Transfer Station / Landfill
Transfer Station / Landfill
From October 1 to October 31, Pottawatomie County residents can drop off passenger tires and refrigeration appliances at no cost. You will be asked for your address before you can drop off the items.
You must be able to tell us what you are bringing or provide us with a list of items.
There will be a fee of 50% of the normal rate for all other non-passenger vehicle tires. All loads must be secured or tarped.
No-Cost Items eligible for drop off:
Pickup & Passenger tires (with or without rim)
Refrigerators
Freezers
Air Conditioner Units
Dehumidifiers
Coolers
List of Half Price Items :
Semi Tires (with or without rim)
Skid Steer Tires (with or without rim)
Small Tractor Tires (with or without rim)
Large Tractor Tires (with or without rim)
Extra Large Tractor Tires (with or without rim)
Transfer Station hours are 8:30 am - 4:15 pm Monday through Saturday, excluding holidays. The Transfer Station will be closed Monday, October 12, 2026.
Business and commercial haulers are excluded from the amnesty program.
Please call 785-456-9706 with questions.
Transfer Station
The transfer station is operated to provide for safe disposal of solid waste. The station will accept household hazardous waste, e-waste, construction debris, tires, and used oil.
For a more detailed listing of prices, view the 2026 Uniform Fee Schedule (PDF) .
Cash, Check or Credit Cards Accepted.
View the Landfill E-Waste (PDF) document for items considered e-waste.
ALL LOADS must be in facility by 4:15 p.m. NO Exceptions.

Lithium batteries can cause fires in trash cans and garbage trucks if they are not properly disposed of. Use tape (the EPA recommends using electrical tape) or plastic bags to cover the battery terminals completely isolate the device or battery to prevent terminal contact and sparks. If a lithium battery is leaking or bulging, remove the battery from the device and place it in an area away from flammable materials. Place it in a fire resistant container with sand or other extinguishing agent.
Take the battery and device, if the battery is not removable, to the Transfer Station/Landfill for proper disposal.
The Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE) has more information on lithium-ion battery disposal.
